source.primary_witnesses: MT BHS Codex Leningradensis — entirely Aramaic. Belshazzar's feast + the writing on the wall + Belshazzar's death. SECONDARY: 4Q112 (Daniela) + 4Q113 (Danielb) preserve fragments of ch 5. TERTIARY: OG presents a substantially shorter and reorganized version; Theodotion-Greek conforms more closely to MT. The cuneiform Nabonidus Chronicle attests Belshazzar as crown prince + regent of Babylon (553-543 BCE); Belshazzar was NOT 'son of Nebuchadnezzar' in literal genealogy (he was son of Nabonidus, the usurper-king) — the literary genealogy in Dan 5 is dynastic-symbolic, not biological.
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against BHS apparatus + DJD XVI 2000 + Ziegler-Munnich 1999.
source.fetchedFrom: BHS; Ulrich DJD XVI 2000; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999.
source.citation: BHS (Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft 1997); Ulrich et al. 2000 DJD XVI; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999 Septuaginta XVI.2; Nabonidus Chronicle (BM 35382).
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 5 — ARAMAIC, the writing on the wall. The MENE MENE TEKEL UPHARSIN inscription (v 25) is one of the most famous textual cruxes in the Hebrew Bible; the four Aramaic words are weight-measures (mina, mina, shekel, half-shekels) that simultaneously encode verbs (counted, counted, weighed, divided) AND ethnic-imperial puns (Persia + Medes). The Aramaic punning is a virtuosic display of trilingual ANE wordplay that does not survive translation. Belshazzar was the historical co-regent (not king) during Nabonidus's Teima sojourn; the Dan 5 framing of him as 'king' is consistent with his de-facto regency. The chapter's date is 539 BCE, the night Babylon fell to Cyrus the Persian (12-13 October 539, per Nabonidus Chronicle obverse iii).

verses.text: בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֗א עֲבַד֙ לְחֶ֣ם רַ֔ב לְרַבְרְבָנ֖וֹהִי אֲלַ֑ף וְלָקֳבֵ֥ל אַלְפָּ֖א חַמְרָ֥א שָׁתֵֽה׃
verses.translit: Bēlšaʾṣṣar malkāʾ ʿăḇaḏ ləḥem raḇ lə-raḇrəḇānōhî ʾălap̄ wə-lā-qoḇēl ʾalpāʾ ḥamrāʾ šāṯēh
verses.notes: **King Belshazzar made a great feast for a thousand of his lords, and drank wine in front of the thousand.** **NAME**: בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר (Bēlšaʾṣṣar) = Akkadian *Bēl-šar-uṣur* 'Bel protect the king'. Historically Belshazzar was co-regent/crown prince under Nabonidus, attested in the Nabonidus Chronicle + the Verse Account of Nabonidus. The 'thousand lords' frames imperial-decadent scale; the king's public wine-drinking sets the hubris register.

verses.text: בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֞ר אֲמַ֣ר ׀ בִּטְעֵ֣ם חַמְרָ֗א לְהַיְתָיָה֙ לְמָאנֵי֙ דַּהֲבָ֣א וְכַסְפָּ֔א דִּ֤י הַנְפֵּק֙ נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר אֲב֔וּהִי מִן־הֵיכְלָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וְיִשְׁתּ֣וֹן בְּה֗וֹן מַלְכָּא֙ וְרַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי שֵׁגְלָתֵ֖הּ וּלְחֵנָתֵֽהּ׃
verses.translit: Bēlšaʾṣṣar ʾămar bi-ṭʿēm ḥamrāʾ lə-haytāyāh lə-mānê dahăḇāʾ wə-ḵaspāʾ dī hanpēq Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar ʾăḇūhî min-hêḵəlāʾ dī ḇî-Yərūšəlem wə-yištōn bə-hōn malkāʾ wə-raḇrəḇānōhî šēḡəlāṯēh ū-lə-ḥēnāṯēh
verses.notes: **Belshazzar, when he tasted the wine, commanded that the vessels of gold and of silver which Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem be brought, so that the king and his lords, his wives, and his concubines might drink from them.** **THE SACRILEGE**: the Jerusalem temple-vessels (taken in 587 BCE per 2 Kgs 25:14-15 / Jer 52:18-19) are profaned in drinking-vessel use. 'Father' (אֲבוּהִי ʾăḇūhî) is dynastic, not biological — Belshazzar was Nabonidus's son. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Ezra 1:7-11, 5:14, 6:5 (return of temple vessels) — the vessels are theological-symbol of YHWH-presence-portable; their profanation triggers immediate judgment. Cf. 1 Cor 11:27-30 (Paul on unworthy partaking) shares the sacred-vessel-profanation structural motif.

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֗יִן הַיְתִיו֙ מָאנֵ֣י דַהֲבָ֔א דִּ֣י הַנְפִּ֗קוּ מִן־הֵֽיכְלָ֛א דִּֽי־בֵ֥ית אֱלָהָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירֽוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וְאִשְׁתִּ֣יו בְּה֗וֹן מַלְכָּא֙ וְרַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי שֵׁגְלָתֵ֖הּ וּלְחֵנָתֵֽהּ׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin haytîw mānê ḏahăḇāʾ dī hanpiqū min-hêḵəlāʾ dî-ḇêṯ ʾĕlāhāʾ dī ḇî-Yərūšəlem wə-ʾištîw bə-hōn malkāʾ wə-raḇrəḇānōhî šēḡəlāṯēh ū-lə-ḥēnāṯēh
verses.notes: **Then they brought in the golden vessels which had been taken out of the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem; and the king and his lords, his wives, and his concubines drank from them.**

verses.text: אִשְׁתִּ֖יו חַמְרָ֑א וְ֠שַׁבַּ֠חוּ לֵֽאלָהֵ֞י דַּהֲבָ֧א וְכַסְפָּ֛א נְחָשָׁ֥א פַרְזְלָ֖א אָעָ֥א וְאַבְנָֽא׃
verses.translit: ʾištîw ḥamrāʾ wə-šabbaḥū lê-ʾlāhê dahăḇāʾ wə-ḵaspāʾ nəḥāšāʾ p̄arzəlāʾ ʾāʿāʾ wə-ʾaḇnāʾ
verses.notes: **They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.** **THE SIX-MATERIAL LIST**: gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, stone — directly recalls the four-material statue of ch 2 (gold, silver, bronze, iron) plus wood + stone. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Deut 4:28, 28:36, 28:64 (idols of wood and stone); cf. Rev 9:20 (the unrepentant 'continue to worship demons, and idols of gold and silver and bronze and stone and wood'). The Revelation list is structurally identical to Dan 5:4 — direct inheritance.

verses.text: בַּהּ־שַׁעֲתָ֗ה נפקו נְפַ֙קָה֙ אֶצְבְּעָן֙ דִּ֣י יַד־אֱנָ֔שׁ וְכָֽתְבָן֙ לָקֳבֵ֣ל נֶבְרַשְׁתָּ֔א עַל־גִּירָ֕א דִּֽי־כְתַ֥ל הֵיכְלָ֖א דִּ֣י מַלְכָּ֑א וּמַלְכָּ֣א חָזֵ֔ה פַּ֥ס יְדָ֖ה דִּ֥י כָתְבָֽה׃
verses.translit: bah-šaʿăṯāh nəp̄aqāh ʾeṣbəʿān dī yaḏ-ʾĕnāš wə-ḵāṯəḇān lā-qoḇēl neḇraštāʾ ʿal-gîrāʾ dî-ḵəṯal hêḵəlāʾ dī malkāʾ ū-malkāʾ ḥāzēh pas yəḏāh dî ḵāṯəḇāh
verses.notes: **Immediately the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall of the king's palace, opposite the lampstand; and the king saw the hand as it wrote.** **THE WRITING ON THE WALL** — one of the most iconic scenes in scripture. **TERM**: גִּירָא (gîrāʾ 'plaster/whitewash') — the wall-surface in the lamplit hall. The 'opposite the lampstand' (לָקֳבֵל נֶבְרַשְׁתָּא lā-qoḇēl neḇraštāʾ) places the writing under direct light. **CROSS-CORPUS**: the disembodied-hand-of-God writing motif: cf. Exod 31:18 (finger of God writing the tablets); cf. John 8:6, 8:8 (Jesus writes on the ground at the adulteress-pericope) — possibly a deliberate Dan 5:5 allusion. Qere-ketiv: נפקו/נְפַקָה (qere).

verses.text: אֱדַ֤יִן מַלְכָּא֙ זִיוֹ֣הִי שְׁנ֔וֹהִי וְרַעיֹנֹ֖הִי יְבַהֲלוּנֵּ֑הּ וְקִטְרֵ֤י חַרְצֵהּ֙ מִשְׁתָּרַ֔יִן וְאַ֨רְכֻבָּתֵ֔הּ דָּ֥א לְדָ֖א נָֽקְשָֽׁן׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin malkāʾ zîwōhî šənōhî wə-raʿyōnōhî yəḇahălūnnēh wə-qiṭrê ḥarṣēh mištārayin wə-ʾarkubbāṯēh dāʾ lə-ḏāʾ nāqəšān
verses.notes: **Then the king's color changed, and his thoughts alarmed him; the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees knocked together.** **VISCERAL TERROR-DESCRIPTION**: 'joints of loins loosed' (קִטְרֵי חַרְצֵהּ מִשְׁתָּרַיִן qiṭrê ḥarṣēh mištārayin) = involuntary urination/incontinence under terror. Knees knocking together: iconic somatic-fear description. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Isa 21:3-4 (the prophet's loins-terror at Babylon's fall); cf. Nah 2:10 ('hearts melt, knees totter, loins shake'). The Daniel scene literarily fulfills the prophetic visions of Babylon's fall.

verses.text: קָרֵ֤א מַלְכָּא֙ בְּחַ֔יִל לְהֶֽעָלָה֙ לְאָ֣שְׁפַיָּ֔א כשדיא כַּשְׂדָּאֵ֖י וְגָזְרַיָּ֑א עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֣ר ׀ לְחַכִּימֵ֣י בָבֶ֗ל דִּ֣י כָל־אֱ֠נָשׁ דִּֽי־יִקְרֵ֞ה כְּתָבָ֣ה דְנָ֗ה וּפִשְׁרֵהּ֙ יְחַוִּנַּ֔נִי אַרְגְּוָנָ֣א יִלְבַּ֗שׁ והמונכא וְהַֽמְנִיכָ֤א דִֽי־דַהֲבָא֙ עַֽל־צַוְּארֵ֔הּ וְתַלְתִּ֥י בְמַלְכוּתָ֖א יִשְׁלַֽט׃
verses.translit: qārēʾ malkāʾ bə-ḥayil lə-heʿālāh lə-ʾāšəpayyāʾ kaśdāʾê wə-ḡāzərayyāʾ ʿănēh malkāʾ wə-ʾāmar lə-ḥakkîmê Bāḇel dī ḵol-ʾĕnāš dî-yiqrēh kəṯāḇāh ḏənāh ū-p̄išrēh yəḥawwinnannî ʾargəwānāʾ yilbaš wə-hamnîḵāʾ ḏî-ḏahăḇāʾ ʿal-ṣawwərēh wə-ṯalti ḇə-malḵūṯāʾ yišlaṭ
verses.notes: **The king cried aloud to bring in the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the astrologers; the king said to the wise men of Babylon: 'Whoever reads this writing and shows me its interpretation shall be clothed with purple, have a chain of gold about his neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.'** **THE 'THIRD RULER' DETAIL**: historically precise — Belshazzar himself was second under Nabonidus, so 'third' is the highest rank he can offer. This is a confirming-detail favoring memory of historical co-regency. **TERMS**: אַרְגְּוָן (ʾargəwān 'purple') — Persian loanword from *raga-vana*. הַמְנִיךְ (hamnîḵ 'chain/necklace') — Persian loanword. Qere-ketiv: כשדיא/כַּשְׂדָּאֵי; והמונכא/וְהַמְנִיכָא.

verses.text: אֱדַ֙יִן֙ עללין עָֽלִּ֔ין כֹּ֖ל חַכִּימֵ֣י מַלְכָּ֑א וְלָֽא־כָהֲלִ֤ין כְּתָבָא֙ לְמִקְרֵ֔א ופשרא וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ לְהוֹדָעָ֥ה לְמַלְכָּֽא׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin ʿāllîn kōl ḥakkîmê malkāʾ wə-lāʾ-ḵāhălîn kəṯāḇāʾ lə-miqrēʾ ū-p̄išrēh lə-hōḏāʿāh lə-malkāʾ
verses.notes: **Then all the king's wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or make known to the king the interpretation.** Qere-ketiv: עללין/עָלִּין; ופשרא/וּפִשְׁרֵה.

verses.text: אֱ֠דַיִן מַלְכָּ֤א בֵלְשַׁאצַּר֙ שַׂגִּ֣יא מִתְבָּהַ֔ל וְזִיוֹ֖הִי שָׁנַ֣יִן עֲל֑וֹהִי וְרַבְרְבָנ֖וֹהִי מִֽשְׁתַּבְּשִֽׁין׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin malkāʾ Bēlšaʾṣṣar śaggîʾ miṯbāhal wə-zîwōhî šānayin ʿălōhî wə-raḇrəḇānōhî mištabbəšîn
verses.notes: **Then King Belshazzar was greatly alarmed, and his color changed; and his lords were perplexed.**

verses.text: מַלְכְּתָ֕א לָקֳבֵ֨ל מִלֵּ֤י מַלְכָּא֙ וְרַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי לְבֵ֥ית מִשְׁתְּיָ֖א עללת עֲלַ֑ת עֲנָ֨ת מַלְכְּתָ֜א וַאֲמֶ֗רֶת מַלְכָּא֙ לְעָלְמִ֣ין חֱיִ֔י אַֽל־יְבַהֲלוּךְ֙ רַעְיוֹנָ֔ךְ וְזִיוָ֖יךְ אַל־יִשְׁתַּנּֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: malkəṯāʾ lā-qoḇēl millê malkāʾ wə-raḇrəḇānōhî lə-ḇêṯ mištəyāʾ ʿălaṯ ʿănāṯ malkəṯāʾ wa-ʾămereṯ malkāʾ lə-ʿāləmîn ḥĕyî ʾal-yəḇahălūḵ raʿyōnāḵ wə-zîwāyḵ ʾal-yištannō
verses.notes: **The queen, because of the words of the king and his lords, came into the banqueting hall; the queen said: 'O king, live forever! Let not your thoughts alarm you or your color change.'** **THE QUEEN**: probably the queen-mother (Nitocris of Babylon per Herodotus 1.188) rather than a wife — she has authoritative knowledge of Daniel and Nebuchadnezzar-era court. Qere-ketiv: עללת/עֲלַת.

verses.text: אִיתַ֨י גְּבַ֜ר בְּמַלְכוּתָ֗ךְ דִּ֠י ר֣וּחַ אֱלָהִ֣ין קַדִּישִׁין֮ בֵּהּ֒ וּבְיוֹמֵ֣י אֲב֗וּךְ נַהִיר֧וּ וְשָׂכְלְתָנ֛וּ וְחָכְמָ֥ה כְּחָכְמַת־אֱלָהִ֖ין הִשְׁתְּכַ֣חַת בֵּ֑הּ וּמַלְכָּ֤א נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּר֙ אֲב֔וּךְ רַ֧ב חַרְטֻמִּ֣ין אָֽשְׁפִ֗ין כַּשְׂדָּאִין֙ גָּזְרִ֔ין הֲקִימֵ֖הּ אֲב֥וּךְ מַלְכָּֽא׃
verses.translit: ʾîtay gəḇar bə-malḵūṯāḵ dī rûaḥ ʾĕlāhîn qaddîšîn bēh ū-ḇə-yōmê ʾăḇūḵ nahîrū wə-śoḵləṯānū wə-ḥoḵmāh kə-ḥoḵmaṯ-ʾĕlāhîn hištəḵaḥaṯ bēh ū-malkāʾ Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar ʾăḇūḵ raḇ ḥarṭummîn ʾāšəpîn kaśdāʾîn gāzərîn hăqîmēh ʾăḇūḵ malkāʾ
verses.notes: **'There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; in the days of your father light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, were found in him; and King Nebuchadnezzar your father — your father the king, I say — made him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and astrologers.'** Daniel is identified by his chief-of-magicians title from 2:48 + 4:9.

verses.text: כָּל־קֳבֵ֡ל דִּ֣י ר֣וּחַ ׀ יַתִּירָ֡ה וּמַנְדַּ֡ע וְשָׂכְלְתָנ֡וּ מְפַשַּׁ֣ר חֶלְמִין֩ וַֽאַֽחֲוָיַ֨ת אֲחִידָ֜ן וּמְשָׁרֵ֣א קִטְרִ֗ין הִשְׁתְּכַ֤חַת בֵּהּ֙ בְּדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל דִּֽי־מַלְכָּ֥א שָׂם־שְׁמֵ֖הּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֑ר כְּעַ֛ן דָּנִיֵּ֥אל יִתְקְרֵ֖י וּפִשְׁרָ֥ה יְהַֽחֲוֵֽה׃
verses.translit: kol-qŏḇēl dī rûaḥ yattîrāh ū-mandaʿ wə-śoḵləṯānū məp̄aššar ḥelmîn wa-ʾaḥăwāyaṯ ʾăḥîḏān ū-məšārēʾ qiṭrîn hištəḵaḥaṯ bēh bə-Dāniyyēʾl dî-malkāʾ śām-šəmēh Bēlṭəšaʾṣṣar kəʿan Dāniyyēʾl yiṯqərēʾ ū-p̄išrāh yə-haḥăwēh
verses.notes: **'Because an excellent spirit, knowledge, and understanding to interpret dreams, explain riddles, and solve problems were found in this Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Let Daniel now be called, and he will show the interpretation.'** **TERM**: מְשָׁרֵא קִטְרִין (məšārēʾ qiṭrîn 'loosener of knots') — Aramaic idiom for solving difficult problems; the same idiom recurs in later Aramaic-magical-incantation contexts.

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֙יִן֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל הֻעַ֖ל קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֑א עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֣ר לְדָנִיֵּ֗אל אנתה־ה֤וּא אַנְתְּ־ה֤וּא דָנִיֵּאל֙ דִּֽי־מִן־בְּנֵ֤י גָלוּתָא֙ דִּ֣י יְה֔וּד דִּ֤י הַיְתִי֙ מַלְכָּ֣א אַ֔בִי מִן־יְהֽוּד׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin Dāniyyēʾl huʿal qŏdām malkāʾ ʿănēh malkāʾ wə-ʾāmar lə-Dāniyyēʾl ʾant-hūʾ Dāniyyēʾl dî-min-bənê ḡālūṯāʾ dī Yəhūḏ dî haytî malkāʾ ʾaḇî min-Yəhūḏ
verses.notes: **Then Daniel was brought in before the king. The king said: 'Are you that Daniel, one of the exiles of Judah, whom the king my father brought from Judah?'** Daniel-as-exile is foregrounded — the political-marginal identity that nonetheless interprets imperial fate. Qere-ketiv: אנתה־הוא/אַנְתְּ־הוּא.

verses.text: וְשִׁמְעֵ֣ת עליך עֲלָ֔ךְ דִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ אֱלָהִ֖ין בָּ֑ךְ וְנַהִיר֧וּ וְשָׂכְלְתָנ֛וּ וְחָכְמָ֥ה יַתִּירָ֖ה הִשְׁתְּכַ֥חַת בָּֽךְ׃
verses.translit: wə-šimʿēṯ ʿălāḵ dī rûaḥ ʾĕlāhîn bāḵ wə-nahîrū wə-śoḵləṯānū wə-ḥoḵmāh yattîrāh hištəḵaḥaṯ bāḵ
verses.notes: **'I have heard of you that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that light and understanding and excellent wisdom are found in you.'** Qere-ketiv: עליך/עֲלָךְ.

verses.text: וּכְעַ֞ן הֻעַ֣לּוּ קָֽדָמַ֗י חַכִּֽימַיָּא֙ אָֽשְׁפַיָּ֔א דִּֽי־כְתָבָ֤ה דְנָה֙ יִקְר֔וֹן וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ לְהוֹדָעֻתַ֑נִי וְלָֽא־כָהֲלִ֥ין פְּשַֽׁר־מִלְּתָ֖א לְהַחֲוָיָֽה׃
verses.translit: ū-ḵəʿan huʿallū qodāmay ḥakkîmayyāʾ ʾāšəpayyāʾ dî-ḵəṯāḇāh ḏənāh yiqrōn ū-p̄išrēh lə-hōḏāʿuṯanî wə-lāʾ-ḵāhălîn pəšar-milləṯāʾ lə-haḥăwāyāh
verses.notes: **'Now the wise men, the enchanters, have been brought in before me to read this writing and make known to me its interpretation; but they could not show the interpretation of the matter.'**

verses.text: וַאֲנָה֙ שִׁמְעֵ֣ת עליך עֲלָ֔ךְ דִּֽי־תוכל תִיכּ֥וּל פִּשְׁרִ֛ין לְמִפְשַׁ֖ר וְקִטְרִ֣ין לְמִשְׁרֵ֑א כְּעַ֡ן הֵן֩ תוכל תִּכ֨וּל כְּתָבָ֜א לְמִקְרֵ֗א וּפִשְׁרֵהּ֙ לְהוֹדָ֣עֻתַ֔נִי אַרְגְּוָנָ֣א תִלְבַּ֗שׁ והמונכא וְהַֽמְנִיכָ֤א דִֽי־דַהֲבָא֙ עַֽל־צַוְּארָ֔ךְ וְתַלְתָּ֥א בְמַלְכוּתָ֖א תִּשְׁלַֽט׃
verses.translit: wa-ʾănāh šimʿēṯ ʿălāḵ dî-ṯikkūl pišrîn lə-mip̄šar wə-qiṭrîn lə-mišrēʾ kəʿan hēn tikkūl kəṯāḇāʾ lə-miqrēʾ ū-p̄išrēh lə-hōḏāʿuṯanî ʾargəwānāʾ ṯilbaš wə-hamnîḵāʾ ḏî-ḏahăḇāʾ ʿal-ṣawwərāḵ wə-ṯaltāʾ ḇə-malḵūṯāʾ tišlaṭ
verses.notes: **'But I have heard of you that you can give interpretations and solve problems. Now if you can read the writing and make known to me its interpretation, you shall be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold about your neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.'** Qere-ketiv (multiple): עליך/עֲלָךְ; תוכל/תִיכּוּל; תוכל/תִּכוּל; והמונכא/וְהַמְנִיכָא.

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֜יִן עָנֵ֣ה דָנִיֵּ֗אל וְאָמַר֙ קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֔א מַתְּנָתָךְ֙ לָ֣ךְ לֶֽהֶוְיָ֔ן וּנְבָ֥זְבְּיָתָ֖ךְ לְאָחֳרָ֣ן הַ֑ב בְּרַ֗ם כְּתָבָא֙ אֶקְרֵ֣א לְמַלְכָּ֔א וּפִשְׁרָ֖א אֲהוֹדְעִנֵּֽהּ׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin ʿănēh Dāniyyēʾl wə-ʾāmar qŏdām malkāʾ mattənāṯāḵ lāḵ lehĕwyān ū-nəḇāzəbəyāṯāḵ lə-ʾoḥŏrān haḇ bəram kəṯāḇāʾ ʾeqrēʾ lə-malkāʾ ū-p̄išrāʾ ʾă-hōḏəʿinnēh
verses.notes: **Then Daniel answered the king: 'Let your gifts be for yourself, and give your rewards to another; nevertheless I will read the writing to the king, and make known to him the interpretation.'** **THE PROPHETIC-INTEGRITY REFUSAL**: cf. Num 22 (Balaam refuses Balak's payments initially); cf. 2 Kgs 5:16 (Elisha refuses Naaman's gifts) — the prophet-as-uncorruptible-by-imperial-gold trope.

verses.text: אנתה אַ֖נְתְּ מַלְכָּ֑א אֱלָהָא֙ עליא עִלָּאָ֔ה מַלְכוּתָ֤א וּרְבוּתָא֙ וִיקָרָ֣א וְהַדְרָ֔ה יְהַ֖ב לִנְבֻכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר אֲבֽוּךְ׃
verses.translit: ʾant malkāʾ ʾĕlāhāʾ ʿillāʾāh malḵūṯāʾ ū-rəḇūṯāʾ wî-qārāʾ wə-haḏrāh yəhaḇ li-Nəḇūḵaḏneṣṣar ʾăḇūḵ
verses.notes: **'O king, the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father kingship and greatness and glory and majesty.'** Daniel begins with the ch 4 narrative-precedent. Qere-ketiv: אנתה/אַנְתְּ; עליא/עִלָּאָה.

verses.text: וּמִן־רְבוּתָא֙ דִּ֣י יְהַב־לֵ֔הּ כֹּ֣ל עַֽמְמַיָּ֗א אֻמַּיָּא֙ וְלִשָּׁ֣נַיָּ֔א הֲו֛וֹ זאעין זָיְעִ֥ין וְדָחֲלִ֖ין מִן־קֳדָמ֑וֹהִי דִּֽי־הֲוָ֨ה צָבֵ֜א הֲוָ֣ה קָטֵ֗ל וְדִֽי־הֲוָ֤ה צָבֵא֙ הֲוָ֣ה מַחֵ֔א וְדִֽי־הֲוָ֤ה צָבֵא֙ הֲוָ֣ה מָרִ֔ים וְדִֽי־הֲוָ֥ה צָבֵ֖א הֲוָ֥ה מַשְׁפִּֽיל׃
verses.translit: ū-min-rəḇūṯāʾ dī yəhaḇ-lēh kōl ʿammə-mayyāʾ ʾummayyāʾ wə-liššānayyāʾ hăwō zāyəʿîn wə-ḏāḥălîn min-qodāmōhî dî-hăwāh ṣāḇēʾ hăwāh qāṭēl wə-ḏî-hăwāh ṣāḇēʾ hăwāh maḥēʾ wə-ḏî-hăwāh ṣāḇēʾ hăwāh mārîm wə-ḏî-hăwāh ṣāḇēʾ hăwāh mašpîl
verses.notes: **'And because of the greatness that he gave him, all peoples, nations, and languages trembled and feared before him; whom he would he slew, and whom he would he kept alive; whom he would he raised up, and whom he would he put down.'** **ARBITRARY-SOVEREIGN-POWER FORMULA** — the four-fold killed/spared/raised/abased structure is the classic ANE divine-king prerogative. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. 1 Sam 2:6-7 (Hannah's song: 'The LORD kills and brings to life; he brings down to Sheol and raises up'); cf. Deut 32:39. Qere-ketiv: זאעין/זָיְעִין.

verses.text: וּכְדִי֙ רִ֣ם לִבְבֵ֔הּ וְרוּחֵ֖הּ תִּֽקְפַ֣ת לַהֲזָדָ֑ה הָנְחַת֙ מִן־כָּרְסֵ֣א מַלְכוּתֵ֔הּ וִֽיקָרָ֖ה הֶעְדִּ֥יו מִנֵּֽהּ׃
verses.translit: ū-ḵə-ḏî rim liḇḇēh wə-rūḥēh tiqp̄aṯ la-hăzāḏāh honḥaṯ min-korsēʾ malḵūṯēh wî-qārāh heʿdîw minnēh
verses.notes: **'But when his heart was lifted up and his spirit was hardened so that he dealt proudly, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and his glory was taken from him.'** Recap of ch 4 fall.

verses.text: וּמִן־בְּנֵי֩ אֲנָשָׁ֨א טְרִ֜יד וְלִבְבֵ֣הּ ׀ עִם־חֵיוְתָ֣א שוי שַׁוִּ֗יְו וְעִם־עֲרָֽדַיָּא֙ מְדוֹרֵ֔הּ עִשְׂבָּ֤א כְתוֹרִין֙ יְטַ֣עֲמוּנֵּ֔הּ וּמִטַּ֥ל שְׁמַיָּ֖א גִּשְׁמֵ֣הּ יִצְטַבַּ֑ע עַ֣ד דִּֽי־יְדַ֗ע דִּֽי־שַׁלִּ֞יט אֱלָהָ֤א עליא עִלָּאָה֙ בְּמַלְכ֣וּת אֲנָשָׁ֔א וּלְמַן־דִּ֥י יִצְבֵּ֖ה יְהָקֵ֥ים עֲלַֽיהּ׃
verses.translit: ū-min-bənê ʾănāšāʾ ṭərîḏ wə-liḇḇēh ʿim-ḥêwəṯāʾ šawwîw wə-ʿim-ʿărāḏayyāʾ mə-ḏōrēh ʿiśbāʾ ḵə-ṯōrîn yəṭaʿămūnnēh ū-miṭṭal šəmayyāʾ gišmēh yiṣṭabbaʿ ʿaḏ dî-yəḏaʿ dî-šallîṭ ʾĕlāhāʾ ʿillāʾāh bə-malḵūṯ ʾănāšāʾ ū-lə-man-dî yiṣbēh yə-hāqêm ʿălah
verses.notes: **'He was driven from among the sons of men, and his mind was made like that of a beast; his dwelling was with the wild asses, he was fed grass like an ox, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, until he knew that the Most High God rules the kingdom of men and sets over it whom he will.'** **TERM**: עֲרָדַיָּא (ʿărāḏayyāʾ 'wild asses') — adds a detail not present in ch 4 narrative. Qere-ketiv: שוי/שַׁוִּיְו; עליא/עִלָּאָה.

verses.text: ואנתה וְאַ֤נְתְּ בְּרֵהּ֙ בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֔ר לָ֥א הַשְׁפֵּ֖לְתְּ לִבְבָ֑ךְ כָּל־קֳבֵ֕ל דִּ֥י כָל־דְּנָ֖ה יְדַֽעְתָּ׃
verses.translit: wə-ʾant bərēh Bēlšaʾṣṣar lāʾ hašpēltā liḇḇāḵ kol-qŏḇēl dī ḵol-dənāh yəḏaʿtā
verses.notes: **'But you, his son Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, though you knew all this.'** The condemnation: Belshazzar's failure is the failure of historical-memory. Qere-ketiv: ואנתה/וְאַנְתְּ.

verses.text: וְעַ֣ל מָרֵֽא־שְׁמַיָּ֣א ׀ הִתְרוֹמַ֡מְתָּ וּלְמָֽאנַיָּ֨א דִֽי־בַיְתֵ֜הּ הַיְתִ֣יו קדמיך קָֽדָמָ֗ךְ ואנתה וְאַ֨נְתְּ ורברבניך וְרַבְרְבָנָ֜ךְ שֵֽׁגְלָתָ֣ךְ וּלְחֵנָתָךְ֮ חַמְרָא֮ שָׁתַ֣יִן בְּהוֹן֒ וְלֵֽאלָהֵ֣י כַסְפָּֽא־וְ֠זַהֲבָא נְחָשָׁ֨א פַרְזְלָ֜א אָעָ֣א וְאַבְנָ֗א דִּ֠י לָֽא־חָזַ֧יִן וְלָא־שָׁמְעִ֛ין וְלָ֥א יָדְעִ֖ין שַׁבַּ֑חְתָּ וְלֵֽאלָהָ֞א דִּֽי־נִשְׁמְתָ֥ךְ בִּידֵ֛הּ וְכָל־אֹרְחָתָ֥ךְ לֵ֖הּ לָ֥א הַדַּֽרְתָּ׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿal mārēʾ-šəmayyāʾ hiṯrōmamtā ū-lə-mānayyāʾ ḏî-ḇaytēh haytîw qodāmāḵ wə-ʾant wə-raḇrəḇānāḵ šēḡəlāṯāḵ ū-lə-ḥēnāṯāḵ ḥamrāʾ šāṯayin bə-hōn wə-lê-ʾlāhê ḵaspāʾ-wə-zahăḇāʾ nəḥāšāʾ p̄arzəlāʾ ʾāʿāʾ wə-ʾaḇnāʾ dī lāʾ-ḥāzayin wə-lāʾ-šāməʿîn wə-lāʾ yāḏəʿîn šabbaḥtā wə-lê-ʾlāhāʾ dî-nišmə-ṯāḵ bî-ḏēh wə-ḵol-ʾorḥāṯāḵ lēh lāʾ haddartā
verses.notes: **'You have lifted yourself up against the Lord of heaven; the vessels of his house have been brought before you, and you and your lords, your wives and concubines, have drunk wine from them; and you have praised the gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which do not see or hear or know, but the God in whose hand is your breath, and whose are all your ways, you have not honored.'** **TITLE**: מָרֵא שְׁמַיָּא (mārēʾ šəmayyāʾ 'Lord of heaven') — Aramaic divine title. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Ps 115:5-7, 135:15-17 (idol-mockery: 'they have mouths but do not speak') — the Daniel verse explicitly cites Psalmic anti-idol polemic. Qere-ketiv: קדמיך/קָדָמָךְ; ואנתה/וְאַנְתְּ; ורברבניך/וְרַבְרְבָנָךְ.

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֙יִן֙ מִן־קֳדָמ֔וֹהִי שְׁלִ֖יחַ פַּסָּ֣א דִֽי־יְדָ֑א וּכְתָבָ֥א דְנָ֖ה רְשִֽׁים׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin min-qodāmōhî šəlîaḥ passāʾ ḏî-yəḏāʾ ū-ḵəṯāḇāʾ ḏənāh rəšîm
verses.notes: **'Then from his presence the hand was sent, and this writing was inscribed.'**

verses.text: וּדְנָ֥ה כְתָבָ֖א דִּ֣י רְשִׁ֑ים מְנֵ֥א מְנֵ֖א תְּקֵ֥ל וּפַרְסִֽין׃
verses.translit: ū-ḏənāh ḵəṯāḇāʾ dī rəšîm mənēʾ mənēʾ təqēl ū-p̄arsîn
verses.notes: **And this is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, and PARSIN.** **THE WRITING ON THE WALL — מְנֵא מְנֵא תְּקֵל וּפַרְסִין (mənēʾ mənēʾ təqēl ū-p̄arsîn)**. **TEXTUAL CRUX**: the four Aramaic words are simultaneously: (a) WEIGHT-NAMES — mənēʾ = mina (60 shekels); təqēl = shekel; pəras = half-shekel (the plural form *p̄arsîn* contains the *prs* root); (b) PARTICIPIAL VERB-FORMS that Daniel will exploit in vv 26-28 (mənēh 'counted', təqîl 'weighed', pərîsaṯ 'divided'); (c) ETHNIC-IMPERIAL PUNS — *pəras* puns on *pārās* 'Persia/Persian' (the kingdom-name). **The trilingual wordplay is irreducible to translation.** **CROSS-CORPUS**: this verse is one of the most quoted phrases in Western art-and-literature (the proverbial 'writing on the wall'); Rembrandt's 1635 'Belshazzar's Feast' depicts the moment, with the Aramaic letters written in Hebrew block-script vertically column-by-column per b. Sanhedrin 22a's interpretation. **NOTE ON DOUBLED MENE**: OG transmits only single mənēʾ + təqēl + pəras (three words); some manuscripts of Theodotion likewise. Modern critical scholarship (Collins 1993) tends to read the doubled mənēʾ as later expansion.

verses.text: דְּנָ֖ה פְּשַֽׁר־מִלְּתָ֑א מְנֵ֕א מְנָֽה־אֱלָהָ֥א מַלְכוּתָ֖ךְ וְהַשְׁלְמַֽהּ׃
verses.translit: dənāh pəšar-milləṯāʾ mənēʾ mənāh-ʾĕlāhāʾ malḵūṯāḵ wə-hašləmah
verses.notes: **'This is the interpretation of the matter: MENE — God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.'** First-word interpretation: מְנֵא (mənēʾ) puns on the verb מְנָה (mənāh 'he counted/numbered').

verses.text: תְּקֵ֑ל תְּקִ֥ילְתָּה בְמֹֽאזַנְיָ֖א וְהִשְׁתְּכַ֥חַתְּ חַסִּֽיר׃
verses.translit: təqēl təqîltāh ḇə-mōzanyāʾ wə-hištəḵaḥat ḥassîr
verses.notes: **'TEKEL — you have been weighed in the balances and found wanting.'** Second-word interpretation: תְּקֵל (təqēl) puns on the verb תְּקִיל (təqîl 'he weighed'). **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Job 31:6 ('let me be weighed in a just balance'); cf. Ps 62:9; cf. Egyptian Book of the Dead ch 125 (the weighing-of-the-heart against the feather of maat) — the divine-balance judgment-motif is ANE-wide.

verses.text: פְּרֵ֑ס פְּרִיסַת֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔ךְ וִיהִיבַ֖ת לְמָדַ֥י וּפָרָֽס׃
verses.translit: pərēs pərîsaṯ malḵūṯāḵ wî-hîḇaṯ lə-Māḏay ū-P̄ārās
verses.notes: **'PERES — your kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.'** Third-word interpretation: פְּרֵס (pərēs, singular of the plural פַּרְסִין parsîn) puns simultaneously on (a) the verb פְּרִיסַת (pərîsaṯ 'it has been divided') and (b) פָּרָס (Pārās 'Persia'). The triple-pun is virtuosic. **HISTORICAL NOTE**: Babylon fell to Cyrus the Persian on 12-13 October 539 BCE per the Nabonidus Chronicle. The Median element in 'Medes and Persians' reflects the inherited Median territory in the Persian empire (Cyrus had united Medes and Persians under his rule before taking Babylon).

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֣יִן ׀ אֲמַ֣ר בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֗ר וְהַלְבִּ֤שׁוּ לְדָֽנִיֵּאל֙ אַרְגְּוָנָ֔א והמונכא וְהַֽמְנִיכָ֥א דִֽי־דַהֲבָ֖א עַֽל־צַוְּארֵ֑הּ וְהַכְרִ֣זֽוּ עֲל֔וֹהִי דִּֽי־לֶהֱוֵ֥א שַׁלִּ֛יט תַּלְתָּ֖א בְּמַלְכוּתָֽא׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin ʾămar Bēlšaʾṣṣar wə-halbišū lə-Dāniyyēʾl ʾargəwānāʾ wə-hamnîḵāʾ ḏî-ḏahăḇāʾ ʿal-ṣawwərēh wə-haḵrizū ʿălōhî dî-lehĕwēʾ šallîṭ taltāʾ bə-malḵūṯāʾ
verses.notes: **Then Belshazzar commanded, and Daniel was clothed with purple, a chain of gold was put about his neck, and proclamation was made concerning him that he should be the third ruler in the kingdom.** **NARRATIVE IRONY**: the reward is paid out hours before the kingdom passes to the Persians and Belshazzar dies — Daniel becomes 'third ruler' of a kingdom about to cease. Qere-ketiv: והמונכא/וְהַמְנִיכָא.

verses.text: בֵּ֚הּ בְּלֵ֣ילְיָ֔א קְטִ֕יל בֵּלְאשַׁצַּ֖ר מַלְכָּ֥א כשדיא כַשְׂדָּאָֽה׃
verses.translit: bēh bə-lêləyāʾ qəṭîl Bēlšaʾṣṣar malkāʾ ḵaśdāʾāh
verses.notes: **That very night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed.** **HISTORICAL NOTE**: the Nabonidus Chronicle attests Babylon's peaceful surrender to Ugbaru/Gubaru's forces on the 16th of Tashritu, 539 BCE; Belshazzar's death is not directly attested in the chronicle but is consistent with the regime-change. The 'that very night' chronology is theological-literary: judgment fulfilled within hours. **VERSE NUMBERING**: BHS treats this as v 30 ending ch 5; English Bibles vary — some include the following 'Darius the Mede received the kingdom' as 5:31 (English), others as 6:1 (BHS). This file follows BHS, so 'Darius the Mede received the kingdom' is 6:1 in source-6.json. Qere-ketiv: כשדיא/כַשְׂדָּאָה.
